1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: God, who at many times and in many ways spoke in time past to the fathers by the prophets,
Has in these last days spoken to us by His Son. God has appointed the Son heir of all things. By the Son also God made the worlds.

The Son is the brightness of God's glory, and the express image (exact picture) of His person. The Son upholds all things by the word of His power. When He had by Himself purged (washed away) our sins, He sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.
He is made so much better than the angels, as He has by inheritance received a more excellent name than they have.
For to which of the angels did God ever say: You are My Son, this day have I begotten You (become Your Father)? And again: I will be to Him a Father, and He will be to Me a Son?
And again, when God brings in the firstbegotten (firstborn) into the world, He says: And let all the angels of God worship Him.
And about the angels God says: He makes His angels spirits, and His ministers (servants) a flame of fire.
But to the Son God says: Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. A sceptre (king's rod) of righteousness (what is right) is the sceptre (king's rod) of Your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness (what is right), and hated iniquity (sin). So God, even Your God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness above Your fellows (companions).
And: You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth. And the heavens are the works of Your hands.
They will perish, but You remain. And they all will grow old like a garment (piece of clothing).
And like a vesture (robe) You will fold them up, and they will be changed. But You are the same, and Your years will not fail (end).
But to which of the angels did God ever say: Sit on My right hand, until I make Your enemies Your footstool?
Are they not all ministering (serving) spirits, sent out to minister (serve) for those who will be heirs of salvation?

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V16 follows the KJV: Jesus took on Him the seed of Abraham (became human), not 'helps'.

verses.text: So we should give the more earnest heed (careful attention) to the things which we have heard, so that at no time we let them slip.
For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast (firm), and every transgression (breaking of the law) and disobedience received a just recompence of reward (fair punishment),
How will we escape, if we neglect so great salvation? It first began to be spoken by the Lord. And it was confirmed (proven true) to us by those who heard Him.
God also bore them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with many kinds of miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, as God willed.
For God has not put into subjection (under the control of) the angels the world to come, which we speak about.
But one in a certain place testified (spoke as a witness), saying: What is man, that You are mindful (thinking) of him? Or the son of man, that You visit (care for) him?
You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor, and set him over the works of Your hands.

You have put all things in subjection (under the control) under his feet. For in that God put all in subjection (under control) under him, He left nothing that is not put under him. But now we do not yet see all things put under him.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor. By the grace of God, Jesus should taste death for every man.

For it became (was fitting for) God, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to make the captain (leader) of their salvation perfect (complete) through sufferings.
For both the One who sanctifies (makes holy) and those who are sanctified (made holy) are all of one. For this reason Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers,
Saying: I will declare (tell) Your name to My brothers. In the middle of the church I will sing praise to You.
And again: I will put My trust in Him. And again: Look, I and the children whom God has given Me.

So since the children are partakers (sharers) of flesh and blood, Jesus Himself likewise took part of the same. He did this so that through death He might destroy the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil.
And He did this to deliver (set free) those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage (slavery).
For truly Jesus did not take on Him the nature of angels. But He took on Him the seed of Abraham (became a human being).

So in all things it behoved (was right for) Jesus to be made like His brothers. Then He might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation (bring back to God) for the sins of the people.
For in that Jesus Himself has suffered being tempted, He is able to succour (help) those who are tempted.

3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So, holy brothers, partakers (sharers) of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession (what we say we believe), Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus was faithful to God who appointed Him, as Moses also was faithful in all his house.
For this man Jesus was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, just as the one who has built the house has more honor than the house.
For every house is built by some man. But the One who built all things is God.
And Moses truly was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony (witness) of the things which were to be spoken after.
But Christ was faithful as a Son over His own house. We are His house, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end.
So, as the Holy Spirit says: Today if you will hear His voice,
Do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation (making God angry), in the day of temptation in the wilderness (desert).
There your fathers tempted (tested) Me, proved (tested) Me, and saw My works forty years.
So I was grieved with that generation, and said: They always err (go wrong) in their heart. And they have not known My ways.
So I swore in My wrath (anger): They will not enter into My rest.
Take heed (be careful), brothers, so that there is not in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
But exhort (encourage) one another daily, while it is called Today. Do this so that none of you is hardened through the deceitfulness (lies) of sin.
For we are made partakers (sharers) of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast (firm) to the end.
While it is said: Today if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation (making God angry).
For some, when they had heard, did provoke (make God angry). But not all who came out of Egypt by Moses.
But with whom was God grieved forty years? Was it not with those who had sinned, whose carcases (dead bodies) fell in the wilderness (desert)?
And to whom did God swear that they would not enter into His rest, but to those who did not believe?
So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.

4.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So let us fear, because a promise is left to us of entering into God's rest. Let us fear that any of you should seem to come short of it.
For the gospel (good news) was preached to us, as well as to them. But the word preached did not profit (help) them, because it was not mixed with faith in those who heard it.

For we who have believed do enter into rest. As God said: As I have sworn in My wrath (anger), if they will enter into My rest (they will not enter). Yet the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
For God spoke in a certain place about the seventh day like this: And God rested on the seventh day from all His works.
And in this place again: If they will enter into My rest (they will not enter).
So it remains that some must enter into it. And those to whom it was first preached did not enter in because of unbelief.
Again, God limits (sets) a certain day, saying in David: Today, after so long a time. As it is said: Today if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.
For if Jesus (Joshua) had given them rest, then God would not afterward have spoken of another day.
So there remains a rest to the people of God.
For the one who has entered into God's rest, he also has ceased (stopped) from his own works, as God did from His.
So let us labor (work hard) to enter into that rest, so that no one falls after the same example of unbelief.

For the word of God is quick (living) and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword. It pierces even to the dividing apart of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow. It is a discerner (judge) of the thoughts and intents (plans) of the heart.
There is not any creature that is not manifest (seen clearly) in God's sight. But all things are naked and opened to the eyes of God, with whom we have to do.
So since we have a great high priest, who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession (what we say we believe).
For we do not have a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities (weaknesses). But He was in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
So let us come boldly to the throne of grace, so that we may obtain (receive) mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained (appointed) for men in things pertaining to God. He offers both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can have compassion on the ignorant (those who do not know), and on those who are out of the way, because he himself also is compassed (surrounded) with infirmity (weakness).
And because of this weakness he ought to offer for sins, as for the people, so also for himself.
And no man takes this honor to himself, but the one who is called by God, as Aaron was.
So also Christ did not glorify Himself to be made a high priest. But God glorified Him, who said to Him: You are My Son, today have I begotten You (become Your Father).
As God says also in another place: You are a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec.

In the days of His flesh (life on earth), Christ offered up prayers and supplications (humble requests) with strong crying and tears to God, who was able to save Him from death. And He was heard because He feared (honored God).
Though He was a Son, yet He learned obedience by the things which He suffered.
And being made perfect (complete), He became the author (source) of eternal salvation to all who obey Him.
He was called by God a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
About Him we have many things to say, and hard to explain, since you are dull of hearing (slow to understand).

For when for the time you should be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the first principles (basic lessons) of the oracles (words) of God. You have become such as need milk, and not strong meat (solid food).
For every one who uses milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness (being right with God). For he is a babe (baby).
But strong meat (solid food) belongs to those who are of full age (grown up). By reason of use, they have their senses exercised (trained) to discern (tell apart) both good and evil.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So leaving the principles (first lessons) of the doctrine (teaching) of Christ, let us go on to perfection (being fully grown). Let us not lay again the foundation of repentance (a change of heart) from dead works, and of faith toward God,
Of the doctrine (teaching) of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection (rising) of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
And this we will do, if God permits (allows).
For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened (given light), and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers (sharers) of the Holy Spirit,
And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,

If they fall away, to renew (bring) them again to repentance (a change of heart). For they crucify (put to death on a cross) the Son of God afresh (again) for themselves, and put Him to an open shame.
For the earth which drinks in the rain that comes often on it, and brings out plants that are good for those by whom it is dressed (farmed), receives blessing from God.
But that which bears thorns and briers is rejected, and is near to cursing. Its end is to be burned.
But, beloved (dear friends), we are persuaded of better things of you, and things that go with salvation, though we speak like this.

For God is not unrighteous (unfair) to forget your work and labor of love. You have showed this love toward God's name, in that you have ministered (served) to the saints (holy people), and still do minister (serve).
And we desire that every one of you show the same diligence (hard work) to the full assurance (being sure) of hope to the end.
Then you will not be slothful (lazy), but followers of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For when God made promise to Abraham, because He could swear by no one greater, He swore by Himself,
Saying: Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.
And so, after Abraham had patiently endured, he obtained (received) the promise.
For men truly swear by the greater. And an oath for confirmation (proof) is to them an end of all strife (arguing).
In this way God, wanting to show more abundantly (clearly) to the heirs of promise the immutability (never changing) of His counsel (plan), confirmed (made it sure) by an oath.

This was so that by two immutable (never changing) things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation (comfort). We have fled for refuge (safety) to lay hold on the hope set before us.
We have this hope as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast (firm). It enters into that which is within the veil (curtain).
There the forerunner (one who goes first) has entered for us, that is Jesus, made a high priest forever after the order of Melchisedec.

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him.
Abraham also gave him a tenth part of all. Melchisedec is first, by the meaning of his name, King of righteousness (what is right). And after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace.
He is without father, without mother, without descent (family record), having neither beginning of days, nor end of life. But he is made like the Son of God, and remains a priest continually.
Now consider how great this man was, to whom even the patriarch (forefather) Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils (war treasure).

And truly those of the sons of Levi who receive the office of the priesthood have a commandment to take tithes (a tenth) of the people according to the law. That is, from their brothers, though they come out of the loins (body) of Abraham.
But Melchisedec, whose descent (family line) is not counted from them, received tithes (a tenth) from Abraham, and blessed Abraham, who had the promises.
And without any doubt, the less is blessed by the better.
And here men that die receive tithes (a tenth). But there he receives them, of whom it is witnessed that he lives.
And as I may so say, Levi also, who receives tithes (a tenth), paid tithes (a tenth) in Abraham.
For Levi was still in the loins (body) of his father Abraham, when Melchisedec met him.

So if perfection (being made complete) were by the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
For the One of whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance (served) at the altar.
For it is evident (clear) that our Lord came out of Judah. Moses spoke nothing about priesthood for that tribe.
And it is still far more evident (clear). For after the likeness (looking like) of Melchisedec there rises another priest,
Who is made, not after the law of a carnal (fleshly) commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
For God testifies (speaks as a witness): You are a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec.
For there is truly a disannulling (setting aside) of the commandment going before, because of its weakness and unprofitableness (being useless).
For the law made nothing perfect (complete). But the bringing in of a better hope did. By this hope we draw near to God.
And it was not without an oath that Jesus was made priest.

For those priests were made without an oath. But this priest was made with an oath, by God who said to Him: The Lord swore and will not repent (change His mind): You are a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec.
By so much was Jesus made a surety (guarantee) of a better testament (agreement).
And truly they were many priests, because they were not allowed to continue because of death.
But this Man, because He continues forever, has an unchangeable priesthood.
So He is able also to save them to the uttermost (completely) who come to God by Him. For He ever lives to make intercession (prays to God) for them.
For such a high priest became (was right for) us. He is holy, harmless, undefiled (pure), separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens.
He does not need daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's. For He did this once, when He offered up Himself.
For the law makes men high priests who have infirmity (weakness). But the word of the oath, which was after the law, makes the Son, who is consecrated (set apart) forevermore.

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum (main point): We have such a high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.
He is a minister (servant) of the sanctuary (holy place), and of the true tabernacle (tent), which the Lord pitched (set up), and not man.
For every high priest is ordained (appointed) to offer gifts and sacrifices. So it is necessary that this Man have something also to offer.
For if He were on earth, He should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests who offer gifts according to the law.

They serve the example and shadow of heavenly things. As Moses was admonished (warned) by God when he was about to make the tabernacle (tent): For, see, God says, that you make all things according to the pattern showed to you in the mount (mountain).
But now Jesus has obtained a more excellent ministry (service). By how much also He is the mediator (go-between) of a better agreement, which was established on better promises.
For if that first agreement had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for the second.
For finding fault with them, God says: Look, the days come, says the Lord, when I will make a new agreement with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

It will not be according to the agreement that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. Because they did not continue in My agreement, I did not regard (care for) them, says the Lord.

For this is the agreement that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts. And I will be to them a God, and they will be to Me a people.
And they will not teach every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying: Know the Lord. For all will know Me, from the least to the greatest.
For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness (wrong), and their sins and their iniquities (sins) I will remember no more.
In that God says, A new agreement, He has made the first old. Now what decays and grows old is ready to vanish away.

9.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V16-17 'testament' explained as a will.

verses.text: Then truly the first agreement had also ordinances (rules) of divine service, and an earthly sanctuary (holy place).
For there was a tabernacle (tent) made. In the first part was the candlestick (lampstand), and the table, and the shewbread (holy bread). This is called the sanctuary (holy place).
And after the second veil (curtain), there was the part of the tabernacle (tent) which is called the Holiest of all.

It had the golden censer (incense holder), and the Box of the Agreement covered all around with gold. In it was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables (tablets) of the agreement.
And over it were the cherubims (angels) of glory shadowing the mercyseat (the lid of the Box). We cannot now speak about these things one by one.
Now when these things were made ready like this, the priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle (tent), doing the service of God.
But into the second part went the high priest alone once every year. He did not go without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors (sins) of the people.
The Holy Spirit shows by this that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest (shown clearly), while the first tabernacle (tent) was still standing.

That tent was a figure (picture) for the time then present. In it were offered both gifts and sacrifices that could not make the one who did the service perfect (complete), as pertaining to the conscience.
These stood only in meats (foods) and drinks, and different washings, and carnal (fleshly) ordinances (rules), laid on them until the time of reformation (setting things right).
But Christ came a high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle (tent), not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building.
Christ did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but by His own blood. He entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption (being bought back and set free) for us.
For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of a heifer (young cow) sprinkling the unclean, sanctifies (makes holy) to the purifying (cleaning) of the flesh,
How much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without spot to God, purge (clean) your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

And for this reason Christ is the mediator (go-between) of the new testament (agreement). By means of death, for the redemption (buying back and setting free) of the transgressions (breaking of the law) that were under the first testament (agreement), those who are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
For where a testament (will) is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator (the one who made the will).
For a testament (will) is of force (works) after men are dead. Otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator (the one who made the will) lives.
So neither the first testament (agreement) was dedicated without blood.

For when Moses had spoken every commandment to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop (a plant). And he sprinkled both the book and all the people,
Saying: This is the blood of the testament (agreement) which God has commanded you.
Also he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle (tent) and all the vessels (dishes) of the ministry (service).
And almost all things are by the law purged (made clean) with blood. And without shedding of blood is no remission (forgiveness).
So it was necessary that the patterns (copies) of things in the heavens should be purified (made clean) with these. But the heavenly things themselves are purified with better sacrifices than these.
For Christ has not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures (copies) of the true. But He entered into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.
And He did not enter to offer Himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place every year with blood of others.
For then He must often have suffered since the foundation of the world. But now once in the end of the world He has appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself.
And as it is appointed to men once to die, but after this the judgment,
So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many. And to those who look for Him He will appear the second time without sin to salvation.

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: For the law, having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices make the comers to it perfect (complete). The priests offered those sacrifices year by year continually.
For then would they not have stopped being offered? Because the worshippers once purged (made clean) should have had no more conscience of sins.
But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
So when Christ comes into the world, He says: Sacrifice and offering You did not want, but You have prepared a body for Me.
In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin You have had no pleasure.
Then I said: Look, I come (in the volume (scroll) of the book it is written of Me), to do Your will, O God.
Above, when He said: Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin You did not want, nor had pleasure in them, which are offered by the law,
Then He said: Look, I come to do Your will, O God. He takes away the first, so that He may establish the second.
By the which will we are sanctified (made holy) through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily ministering (serving), and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
But this Man, after He had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God.
From now on He is expecting (waiting) until His enemies are made His footstool.
For by one offering He has perfected (made complete) forever those who are sanctified (made holy).
And the Holy Spirit also is a witness to us. For after He had said before:
This is the agreement that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws into their hearts, and in their minds I will write them.
And their sins and iniquities (sins) I will remember no more.
Now where remission (forgiveness) of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
So, brothers, having boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
By a new and living way, which He has consecrated (opened) for us, through the veil (curtain), that is to say, His flesh,
And having a high priest over the house of God,
Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance (sureness) of faith. Let us have our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold fast the profession (what we say we believe) of our faith without wavering (moving). For God who promised is faithful.
And let us consider one another to provoke (stir up) to love and to good works.

Do not forsake (stop) the assembling (meeting) of ourselves together, as the manner (habit) of some is. But exhort (encourage) one another, and so much the more, as you see the day approaching (coming near).
For if we sin wilfully (on purpose) after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins,
But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation (anger), which will devour (eat up) the adversaries (enemies).
Whoever despised (rejected) Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses.

How much worse punishment, do you suppose, will that one be thought worthy of, who has trodden under foot the Son of God? He has counted the blood of the agreement, with which he was sanctified (made holy), an unholy thing. And he has done despite (insulted) to the Spirit of grace.
For we know the One who has said: Vengeance (paying back) belongs to Me, I will recompense (pay back), says the Lord. And again: The Lord will judge His people.
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But call to remembrance the former days. After you were illuminated (given light), you endured a great fight of afflictions (troubles).
Partly you were made a gazingstock (public show) both by reproaches (insults) and afflictions (troubles). And partly you became companions of those who were treated like that.

For you had compassion on me in my bonds (chains). And you took joyfully the spoiling (taking) of your goods, knowing in yourselves that you have in heaven a better and an enduring (lasting) substance (possession).
So do not cast away your confidence, which has great recompence of reward.
For you have need of patience, so that after you have done the will of God, you might receive the promise.
For yet a little while, and the One who will come will come, and will not tarry (wait).
Now the just (those who are right with God) will live by faith. But if any man draws back, My soul will have no pleasure in him.
But we are not of those who draw back to perdition (destruction). But we are of those who believe to the saving of the soul.

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Now faith is the substance (what is sure) of things hoped for, the evidence (proof) of things not seen.
For by faith the elders obtained a good report.
Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed (made) by the word of God. So the things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.

By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain. By it Abel obtained witness that he was righteous (right with God), God testifying (being a witness) of his gifts. And by it Abel, being dead, still speaks.

By faith Enoch was translated (taken up) so that he should not see death. And he was not found, because God had translated (taken) him. For before his translation (being taken up) he had this testimony (witness), that he pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please God. For whoever comes to God must believe that God is, and that God is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.

By faith Noah, being warned by God of things not seen yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark (big boat) to save his house (family). By the ark he condemned (judged guilty) the world, and became heir of the righteousness (being right with God) which is by faith.
By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he would later receive for an inheritance, obeyed. And he went out, not knowing where he went.
By faith Abraham sojourned (lived as a stranger) in the land of promise, as in a strange country. He dwelt (lived) in tabernacles (tents) with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.
For Abraham looked for a city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
Through faith also Sara herself received strength to conceive seed. And she gave birth to a child when she was past age, because she judged God faithful who had promised.
So there sprang from one man, and him as good as dead, as many as the stars of the sky in number, and as the sand which is by the sea shore, too many to count.

These all died in faith, not having received the promises. But they had seen the promises far off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced (welcomed) them. And they confessed (said) that they were strangers and pilgrims (travelers) on the earth.
For those who say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.
And truly, if they had been thinking of that country from which they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.
But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. So God is not ashamed to be called their God. For He has prepared for them a city.
By faith Abraham, when he was tried (tested), offered up Isaac. And the one who had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
Of whom it was said: In Isaac will your seed be called.
Abraham accounted (judged) that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead. And from there also Abraham received him back in a figure (picture).
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau about things to come.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph. And Jacob worshipped, leaning on the top of his staff (walking stick).
By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel. And he gave commandment about his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw he was a proper (beautiful) child. And they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
By faith Moses, when he was grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
He chose rather to suffer affliction (trouble) with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season (short time).
He esteemed (counted) the reproach (shame) of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt. For he had respect (looked) to the recompence of the reward.
By faith Moses forsook (left) Egypt, not fearing the wrath (anger) of the king. For he endured, as seeing Him who is invisible.
Through faith Moses kept the passover (Passover), and the sprinkling of blood, so that the one who destroyed the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land. When the Egyptians tried to do the same, they were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were circled around for seven days.
By faith the harlot (prostitute) Rahab did not perish with those who did not believe, when she had received the spies with peace.
And what more will I say? For the time would fail me to tell of Gideon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthah. Also of David, and Samuel, and of the prophets.
Through faith they subdued (defeated) kingdoms, worked righteousness (what is right), obtained promises, and stopped the mouths of lions.

They quenched (put out) the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, and out of weakness were made strong. They became valiant (brave) in fight, and turned to flight the armies of the aliens (foreigners).
Women received their dead raised to life again. And others were tortured, not accepting deliverance (being set free), so that they might obtain a better resurrection (rising from the dead).
And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings (whippings). Yes, also of bonds (chains) and imprisonment.

They were stoned. They were sawn in pieces. They were tempted. They were slain with the sword. They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, being destitute (very poor), afflicted (made to suffer), tormented.
The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, did not receive the promise.
God had provided some better thing for us, so that they without us should not be made perfect (complete).

verses.text: So since we also are surrounded with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily besets (wraps around) us. And let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

Looking to Jesus, the author (beginner) and finisher of our faith. For the joy that was set before Him, Jesus endured the cross, despising (thinking nothing of) the shame. And He is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider Jesus, who endured such contradiction (attacks) of sinners against Himself, so that you do not become wearied and faint (lose heart) in your minds.
You have not yet resisted to the point of blood, striving against sin.

And you have forgotten the exhortation (encouragement) which speaks to you as to children: My son, do not despise (look down on) the chastening (correction) of the Lord, and do not faint (lose heart) when you are rebuked (corrected) by Him.
For whom the Lord loves He chastens (corrects). And He scourges (whips) every son whom He receives.
If you endure chastening (correction), God deals with you as with sons. For what son is he whom the father does not chasten (correct)?
But if you are without chastisement (correction), of which all are partakers (sharers), then you are bastards (children not of the family), and not sons.
Also we have had fathers of our flesh (earthly fathers) who corrected us, and we gave them reverence (respect). Should we not much rather be in subjection (obey) the Father of spirits, and live?
For they truly for a few days chastened (corrected) us as they thought best. But God corrects us for our profit (good), so that we might be partakers (sharers) of His holiness.

Now no chastening (correction) for the present seems to be joyous, but grievous (painful). But afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness (being right with God) to those who are exercised (trained) by it.
So lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble (weak) knees.
And make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame is not turned out of the way, but let it rather be healed.
Follow peace with all men, and holiness. Without holiness no man will see the Lord.
Look diligently (carefully) in case any man fails of the grace of God. Look out in case any root of bitterness springing up troubles you, and by it many are defiled (made unclean).
Look out in case there is any fornicator (person who does sexual sin), or profane (unholy) person, like Esau. For one morsel of meat (one meal) Esau sold his birthright (rights of the firstborn son).
For you know how afterward, when Esau wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. For he found no place of repentance (change of mind), though he sought it carefully with tears.
For you have not come to the mount (mountain) that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor to blackness, and darkness, and tempest (storm),
And the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words. Those who heard that voice begged that the word should not be spoken to them any more.
For they could not endure what was commanded: And if so much as a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned, or thrust through with a dart (spear).
And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said: I exceedingly fear and quake (shake).
But you have come to mount Sion (Zion), and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable (too many to count) company of angels,
To the general assembly (great gathering) and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect (complete),
And to Jesus the mediator (go-between) of the new agreement, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaks better things than the blood of Abel.
See that you do not refuse the One who speaks. For if they did not escape who refused the one who spoke on earth, much more we will not escape, if we turn away from the One who speaks from heaven.
God's voice then shook the earth. But now He has promised, saying: Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
And this word, Yet once more, shows the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made. This is so that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
So since we receive a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace. By grace we may serve God acceptably with reverence (respect) and godly fear.
For our God is a consuming fire.

verses.text: Let brotherly love continue.
Do not be forgetful to entertain strangers. For by doing this some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Remember those who are in bonds (chains), as bound with them. And remember those who suffer adversity (hard things), since you yourselves are also in the body.
Marriage is honorable in all, and the bed undefiled (kept pure). But whoremongers (people who do sexual sin) and adulterers (people who have sex with someone else's husband or wife) God will judge.

Let your conversation (way of life) be without covetousness (wanting what belongs to others). And be content with such things as you have. For God has said: I will never leave you, nor forsake (abandon) you.
So we may boldly say: The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man will do to me.
Remember those who have the rule (lead) over you, who have spoken to you the word of God. Follow their faith, considering the end of their conversation (way of life).
Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and today, and forever.

Do not be carried about with different and strange doctrines (teachings). For it is a good thing that the heart be established (made strong) with grace, not with meats (foods). Those who have been occupied in meats (foods) have not been profited (helped).
We have an altar, from which those who serve the tabernacle (tent) have no right to eat.
For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary (holy place) by the high priest for sin, are burned outside the camp.
So Jesus also, so that He might sanctify (make holy) the people with His own blood, suffered outside the gate.
So let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing (carrying) His reproach (shame).
For here we have no continuing city, but we seek one to come.
So by Him let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to His name.
But to do good and to communicate (share), do not forget. For with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Obey those who have the rule (lead) over you, and submit yourselves. For they watch for your souls, as those who must give account. Let them do it with joy, and not with grief. For that would be unprofitable (no help) for you.
Pray for us. For we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly.
But I beg you the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you sooner.
Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting agreement,
Make you perfect (complete) in every good work to do His will. May He work in you what is well pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
And I beg you, brothers, suffer (put up with) the word of exhortation (encouragement). For I have written a letter to you in few words.
Know that our brother Timothy is set at liberty (set free). If he comes shortly, I will see you with him.
Salute (greet) all those who have the rule (lead) over you, and all the saints (holy people). Those of Italy salute (greet) you.
Grace be with you all. Amen.
